headline: High-risk data leakage and capability conflict: slim’s broad filesystem/network powers can expose cognee’s sensitive support data and create unsafe shared-workspace interactions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: cognee ingests documents, workflows, and support history, while slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts and executes shell commands. If slim’s outputs or modified files are fed into cognee’s session memory, prompt-like content can steer downstream behavior. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred from the profiles.
conditions: IF slim writes attacker-controlled text into a file that cognee later ingests
IF an operator copies slim-generated output into cognee without review
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Review any file passed from slim to cognee before ingestion
Disable automatic ingestion of slim outputs into cognee
Use a provenance tag on transferred artifacts
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents, while slim can read the filesystem and has broad network egress plus registry credentials handling. If both share a workspace or credentials, slim can exfiltrate sensitive material to external endpoints. The pairwise path is plausible from the profiles alone, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF cognee and slim share a filesystem or mounted volume
IF slim is given access to files containing support, personal, or finance data
mitigations: Place slim in a separate container with no access to cognee data
Remove registry credentials before running slim
Mount only a minimal read-only input directory
Block outbound network except required registries
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping

C_capability_conflict.rationale: cognee supports multiple instances and session memory, while slim writes the filesystem and executes shell commands in a single target session. If both operate on the same directory, they can overwrite or race on artifacts even though slim does not modify git state. The overlap is real but narrower than high because git conflict is absent.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or mounted volume
IF cognee persists session artifacts that slim also edits
mitigations: Use separate output directories
Make shared inputs read-only
Serialize writes with a lock file
Run slim on a copy of the workspace
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: cognee can produce decisions, workflows, and schema structures, and slim can execute shell commands and act on container artifacts. If slim consumes cognee output as authoritative, a mistaken recommendation can cascade into destructive container changes. There is no evidence of built-in verification between them, so the safer medium rating applies.
conditions: IF slim uses cognee-generated instructions without human verification
IF cognee outputs are treated as commands for shell execution
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Separate analysis output from executable commands
Add a validation step for cognee outputs
Log and diff proposed actions before running slim
requires-engineering: implement schema validation for handoff data

E_compliance.rationale: cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while slim handles registry credentials and certificate private keys and may transmit data over broad network egress. If regulated support data is processed by slim or moved across jurisdictions, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime mismatch, so this remains medium.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data from cognee is passed into slim
IF slim stores or transmits artifacts under a different retention policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of slim inputs
Redact secrets before transfer
Document retention for shared artifacts
Restrict slim to non-sensitive container images
requires-engineering: align data-handling policies across both tools
